# Uppādavāra (Ya 10.2.1)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uppādavāra* (Origination Section) of Yamaka 10 forms the first division of the *pavattivāra* (process section) within the *Yamaka*, the sixth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005]. In the *Yamaka*'s structural framework, the process section examines doctrinal categories through three primary modes of occurrence: origination (*uppādavāra*), cessation (*nirodhavāra*), and origination-cessation combined (*uppādanirodhavāra*) [Anderson 1999; Ronkin 2005]. Methodologically, the *uppādavāra* interrogates whether phenomena are arising with respect to person, to plane or place of existence, and to both person and place together, systematically permuting these inquiries across positive and negative formulations and through the temporal dimensions of present, past, and future [Nyanatiloka 2007; Anderson 1999]. Modern scholars emphasize that this rigorous analytical division reflects an early Buddhist process metaphysics, marking a crucial step toward the Abhidhamma's radical theory of momentariness through the technical distinction of sub-moments of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*) and dissolution (*bhangakkhaṇa*) [Ronkin 2005; Gal 2003].
